title: Lam’s New Logistics Hub Built for Velocity, Resilience, and AI-Era Growth
summary: Lam Research’s new Silicon Valley warehouse speeds semiconductor parts retrieval and strengthens U.S. supply chain resilience.

Lam’s New Logistics Hub Built for Velocity, Resilience, and AI-Era Growth


From left: Katie Marcel, CEO of Innovation Tri-Valley; Livermore Mayor John Marchand; Karthik Rammohan, Lam Senior Vice President; and State Senator Jerry McNerney celebrate the opening of Lam’s new Livermore logistics hub.

- Lam Research has opened its largest U.S. warehouse, a **470,000-square-foot logistics and supply chain hub**
- Investment strengthens Lam’s U.S. footprint and supports **faster, more resilient operations** for customers
- Warehouse workers are supported by an automated storage and retrieval system **** for improved inventory flow, throughput, and space utilization, cutting retrieval time to **less than 30 seconds**


Lam Research has opened its largest U.S. warehouse, a 470,000-square-foot logistics hub designed to strengthen the semiconductor supply chain and support demand for AI-enabled technologies.


- Located in Livermore, California, the facility helps to improve Lam’s ability to move critical parts, absorb shifts in demand, and support customers with greater speed and predictability.


The facility is **more than 10 acres (4.4 hectares)** under one roof, roughly the size of eight football fields—enough room to park 2,000 cars—with inventory retrieval times **12x faster** than current systems.


For Lam, this velocity is not only about moving parts faster. It is about building an operating model that can scale and adapt reliably when customer needs shift.


***Karthik Rammohan** , Lam Senior VP, speaks at the Livermore, CA, warehouse opening ceremony on Sept. 28.*


“This warehouse demonstrates Lam’s commitment to investing in the U.S. as part of our global operations strategy,” said **Karthik Rammohan** , Lam Senior VP of Global Operations and Enterprise Solutions, at the opening ceremony. “We have centralized Lam's California logistics operations into one hub so we can move faster, plan better, and respond to our customers with the speed and accuracy they expect.”


“That is what resilient operations look like in practice, and that is what our customers need from us right now,” he said.


### Lam’s Major Investment in the U.S. Semiconductor Supply Chain


*State Senator **Jerry McNerney** presents Lam Research with a certificate of recognition by the state of California for Lam’s contribution to advanced manufacturing infrastructure, local job growth, and supply chain resilience.*


Lam celebrated the warehouse opening at a September 28 ribbon-cutting ceremony with **Karthik Rammohan, Lam Senior VP; State Senator Jerry McNerney; Livermore Mayor John Marchand; and Katie Marcel, CEO of Innovation Tri-Valley,** along with employees and DHL partners, who will help operate the site.


The new warehouse reinforces Lam’s long-standing presence in California’s semiconductor ecosystem. It is expected to support more than 200 jobs by 2027 and complements the company’s network of R&D, manufacturing, logistics, and office space across northern California.


- The location also provides access to Silicon Valley’s deep talent pool, established suppliers, and the broader semiconductor ecosystem.
- This warehouse will serve Lam’s high-volume manufacturing plant in Livermore, along with the pilot product development at world-class labs at the company’s nearby Fremont headquarters.


### Building Operational Velocity at Scale


An important aspect of the Livermore facility is it centralizes Lam’s California logistics operations into one strategic location.


“With all operations under a single roof, we can create a more agile and efficient operation,” says **Troy Rainey,** director of Lam’s U.S. Warehouse Operations. “This enables us to rapidly reallocate resources as demand and business priorities shift, while eliminating the costs and inefficiencies associated with moving people and materials between multiple facilities.”


That flexibility matters in a market where customers need suppliers that can respond quickly to changing build plans, technology ramps, and demand signals. An adjacent metrology laboratory further strengthens Lam’s outbound delivery responsiveness and regional R&D support.


### Warehouse Automation Powers Faster Inventory Retrieval


At the heart of the facility is a 40,000-square-foot automated storage and retrieval system with 15 robots that shorten part retrieval time from 6 minutes to **less than 30 seconds** .


The system consists of approximately **150,000 storage bins** with the capacity to accommodate more than **500,000 unique part numbers** . This advanced automation solution positions Logistics to support significant future growth while maximizing space utilization.


### Quick Facts About the Warehouse


- Location: Livermore, California
- Purpose: Faster inventory movement and customer delivery support
- Facility size: 470,000+ square feet
- Automation system: 40,000-square-foot automated storage and retrieval system for more than 500,000 unique part numbers
- Robotics: 15 automated robots
- Retrieval time: Less than 30 seconds, 12 times faster than current systems
- Expected jobs supported by 2027: More than 200
